newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay share index down 2.4 pct at mid-session.
newsitem.headline: Bombay share index down 2.4 pct at mid-session.

text.p: Bombay's benchmark stocks index slid 70.24 points or 2.4 percent to 2878.2 at mid-session on Wednesday as punters and funds hammered prices of auto and cement stocks, traders said.
"It's basically auto and cement bashing," said a trader at a European brokerage.
Cement stock ACC was down 150 rupees or 13 percent at 1,006 after its first half results -- announced after market hours on Tuesday -- fell sharply below expectations.

ACC said its net profit fell 56 percent to 550.5 million rupees in the first six months to September 30, 1996 against 1.25 billion rupees. The firm said it could not recover an unprecedented increase in input cost, affecting margins.
Expectations ranged from 800 to 900 million rupees.
ACC shares fell sharply in off-market kerb deals after the results announcement.
Most cement analysts have been bearish about the industry because of oversupply in major markets and a slackening of demand. ACC's results deepened worries.
Index-linked Gujarat Ambuja Cements was also pounded 13.75 rupees or 5.18 percent lower to 251.50.
Auto frontliners TELCO, Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra have also been hit on fears of a prolonged economic slowdown.
Some auto analysts have recommended investors go underweight on the sector.
TELCO shares slipped 20.75 rupees or 6.16 percent to 316, Bajaj fell 38.75 rupees or 4.5 percent to 816.50 and Mahindra shed 12 rupees or 4.2 percent to 275 rupees.
But some auto analysts said they remained bullish on the auto sector.
"Sales growth continues to stay above 20 percent and next fiscal is likely to see a recovery. The extent of the slowdown has been exaggerated," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage.
He said he maintained his buy recommendations on these three stocks.
